Empirical Research Plan  
“Minimum-Wage Increases and Employment in Contiguous-Border Counties, 1990–2006”

-------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------
Method: Two–way fixed-effects Difference-in-Differences (DiD) implemented at the *county-pair*–quarter level.  
Rationale  
• The policy discontinuity occurs at state borders. Counties on opposite sides of the same border share local demand shocks, commuting zones, media markets, and weather, yet face different statutory minimum wages.  
• Conditioning on county-pair fixed effects eliminates all time-invariant cross-border differences (e.g., distance to the nearest metro, soil quality, historical industry mix).  
• Quarter fixed effects purge nationwide shocks (e.g., recessions).  
• Remaining variation is the *within-pair, over-time* change in the minimum-wage differential.  
• This is a clean DiD because no county ever serves as its own control once its own state changes the law; identification comes from contemporaneous neighbors that do not change.

Econometric model (baseline)

ΔlnEmp_ct = β ΔlnMW_ct + γX_ct + μ_pair + τ_t + ε_ct

where Δ is implemented through pair-level differencing or equivalently by including pair fixed effects plus state×year FE.

-------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
• MW_ct ≡ real effective minimum wage in state s containing county c in quarter t  
   (max[federal, state statutory]; CPI-U deflated).  
• Main regressor: ln(MW_ct). Robustness: indicator for “MW increase this quarter.”

Definition of treatment status  
• “Treated” observations are county-quarters in which the own-state minimum wage is strictly higher than the neighbor’s (or rises relative to the neighbor’s).  
• “Control” observations are the simultaneously observed counties on the other side of the border whose minimum wage did not change (or changed less).

Timing / Variation  
• 1990–2006; staggered adoption of higher state minima relative to neighbors. Roughly 120 distinct hikes create the identifying variation.

-------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Trends within County Pairs  
 Absent policy changes, employment in restaurants would have followed the same trend on both sides of the border.  
 Plausibility: Counties in the same local labor market share shocks; we further test with event-study pre-period coefficients.

A2. No Spillovers across the Border at Quarterly Frequency  
 The treatment should not affect employment in the control county in the short run.  
 Plausibility: Cross-border commuting and consumer substitution exist but are small relative to county populations; we probe this with distance-band heterogeneity (exclude pairs <5 miles apart).

A3. Exogeneity of State Minimum-Wage Hikes to Pair-Specific Shocks  
 State legislators do not raise the minimum wage in response to unobserved, *pair-specific* employment trends exactly at the border.  
 Plausibility: Most debates occur at the state level; county-specific lobbying unlikely. We augment with state-specific linear trends.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA) across Non-adjacent Pairs  
 A hike in Washington–Idaho border does not affect Maine. Reasonable given distance.

-------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations
-------------------------------------------------
T1. Cross-Border Spillovers (labor or customers shift)  
 Fix: (i) Exclude the 1–km strip counties in robustness; (ii) run models on *net* pair employment (treated + control) to bound spillovers; (iii) test for jumps in commuting patterns using ACS flows (post-2000).

T2. Differential Pre-Trends  
 Fix: Event-study graphs with leads; include county-pair-specific linear trends; placebo reforms dated two years earlier.

T3. Policy Endogeneity to Local Business Cycles  
 Fix: Add state-year macro controls (GDP growth, political party); instrument MW_ct with interacted *federal* hikes (when only some states are bound) as a robustness IV.

-------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------
```r
# Required packages
library(data.table)   # fast file handling
library(fixest)       # high-dimensional FE
library(ggplot2)      # event study plots

# 1. Load data -------------------------------------------------------------
qwi   <- fread("qwi_restaurants_1990_2006.csv")      # emp by county-qtr
mw    <- fread("state_minwage_qtr_1990_2006.csv")    # real min wage
controls <- fread("county_controls_qtr.csv")         # pop, urate, etc.
pairs <- fread("border_county_pairs.csv")            # each county id, pair_id

# 2. Merge & construct variables ------------------------------------------
dat <- merge(qwi, mw, by = c("state","year","quarter"))
dat <- merge(dat, controls, by = c("fips","year","quarter"))
dat <- merge(dat, pairs, by = "fips")               # adds pair_id

# Log vars
dat[, ln_emp := log(employment)]
dat[, ln_mw  := log(real_mw)]

# 3. Baseline regression ---------------------------------------------------
EST <- feols(ln_emp ~ ln_mw + pop + urate | pair_id + year_quarter, 
             data = dat, cluster = ~pair_id)
summary(EST)

# 4. Event-study (±8 quarters) ---------------------------------------------
dat[, treat_event := year_quarter - minwage_effective_qtr]  # negative = leads
# Keep window
es_dat <- dat[treat_event %between% c(-8,8)]

ES <- feols(ln_emp ~ i(treat_event, ref = -1) | pair_id + year_quarter,
            data = es_dat, cluster = ~pair_id)

iplot(ES, xlab = "Quarters relative to hike", main = "Event study: Restaurants")

# 5. Robustness: drop closest neighbours (<10 miles) -----------------------
dist <- fread("pair_distance_miles.csv") # distance between county centroids
dat2 <- merge(dat, dist, by = "pair_id")
dat2 <- dat2[distance_mi > 10]

EST_rb <- feols(ln_emp ~ ln_mw + pop + urate | pair_id + year_quarter, 
                data = dat2, cluster = ~pair_id)
summary(EST_rb)
```

-------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------
Theory offers ambiguous effects. Monopsony models predict small positive or zero effects; competitive models predict negatives with elasticities near −0.1 to −0.2. Given recent empirical evidence, I expect:  

β ≈ −0.02 to −0.05 (a 10 % ↑ in the minimum wage lowers restaurant employment by 0.2–0.5 %), statistically indistinguishable from zero in most quarters.

-------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist (Self-Assessment, 1 = good, 0 = concern)
1. Clear quasi-experiment? ...................... 1  
2. Parallel-trends evidence (event study)? ...... 0.8  
3. No spillovers/Interference? .................. 0.5  
4. Correct inference (clustered SEs)? ........... 1  
5. Transparency & robustness shown? ............. 0.8  

Overall: credible but spillovers remain the main caveat.
